item.title: Privacy-First AI Home Lab
item.description:
This started with Home Assistant and a Zigbee network about a year ago. I wanted better home automation and an excuse to learn the parts of the stack I had never owned myself. It kept growing. The lab now runs several isolated services under Proxmox, including Home Assistant, Pi-hole, local models through Ollama, and a Hermes assistant.

The interesting part is getting those pieces to work together without handing one AI agent the keys to everything. Hermes handles the conversation. Ollama serves the local model. Home Assistant stays in charge of device actions. I can change or replace one piece without rebuilding the whole setup.

item.title: MTG Scorekeeper
item.description:
I wanted a Magic: The Gathering tracker that I could change whenever a new idea came up, so I built one. It handles life totals, poison, commander damage, and Commander search through Scryfall. The layout works on phones and larger shared screens, which makes it easy to leave in the middle of the table during a game.

This was my hands-on introduction to the modern front-end stack. I learned React and Vite by making something my friends and I could actually use, then kept adding the details that generic counter apps did not handle the way I wanted.

item.title: MTG Scorekeeper Mobile
item.description:
After using the web tracker, I wanted to see what the same idea would feel like as a proper mobile app. I am rebuilding it with React Native and Expo from the ground up.

The app already has game setup, player panels, Commander search, themes, and settings. The most interesting work has been pulling the game rules into reusable logic while giving phones and tablets an interface that feels natural on each screen.
